description: Dive into a casserole dish of pure comfort with our Homemade Baked Mac and Cheese. This classic American dish features tender pasta enveloped in a rich, velvety cheese sauce, all baked to golden, bubbly perfection. It is the ultimate feel-good meal, guaranteed to satisfy every time.

instructions.title: Prepare Pasta
instructions.text: Cook elbow macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well and set aside. Do not rinse the pasta.

instructions.title: Make Roux
instructions.text: In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, melt 1/4 cup unsalted butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until a smooth paste forms. This is your roux.

instructions.title: Whisk in Milk
instructions.text: Gradually whisk in the warmed whole milk, a little at a time, ensuring no lumps form. Continue whisking until the sauce thickens and comes to a gentle simmer, about 5-7 minutes. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.

instructions.title: Add Cheese and Seasonings
instructions.text: Reduce heat to low. Stir in 1.5 cups of shredded sharp cheddar, all the Gruyere, cream cheese (if using), Dijon mustard, salt, pepper, and nutmeg (if using). Stir until all cheese is melted and the sauce is smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.

instructions.title: Combine and Transfer
instructions.text: Add the cooked macaroni to the cheese sauce and stir until evenly coated. Pour the mixture into a greased 9x13 inch baking dish, spreading it out evenly.

instructions.title: Top and Bake
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine Panko breadcrumbs with 2 tablespoons of melted butter. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the macaroni. Top with the remaining 1/2 cup of shredded sharp cheddar cheese. Bake in a preheated oven at 375F (190C) for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and golden brown on top. Let stand for 5-10 minutes before serving.

tips: For the creamiest sauce, ensure your milk is warm before adding it to the roux, and add it gradually while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.

Experiment with different cheese combinations! A mix of sharp cheddar, Gruyere, Fontina, or even a touch of smoked gouda can elevate the flavor. Always shred your own cheese for better melting results.
If preparing ahead, assemble the dish up to the point of baking, cover, and refrigerate. Add an extra 10-15 minutes to the baking time if baking from cold to ensure it heats through completely.
